stem: By the early nineteenth century, education in the United States had become ____ affair: almost every town provided free schools for young children, and many were in the process of building high schools.

The description of humans as having an internal clock is not a (i)____. Or rather, it is—you do not have a tiny watch in your cerebellum—but it also refers to (ii)____, a specialized bundle of cells that regulates cyclical processes.

(i)____ have often shrilled that Australia’s Great Barrier Reef is dying, a result of agricultural runoff from the (ii)____ Queensland coast. In truth, the preservation of the reef (iii)____, a combination of active government intervention and the beneficial effects of responsible tourism.
cols: is something of a success story
colsZh: 建立在不切实际的做法之上
可以说是一个成功案例

stem: Although people often describe the correct trajectory for a thrown or moving object, their efforts to explain that trajectory in terms of physics can reveal ____ understanding of the forces acting on the object.
optsZh: 微妙的；精细的；不易察觉的
简单的；不精巧的；不世故的

stem: Appearing in the midst of so many equivocal comments, this unambiguous statement, whatever its intrinsic merit, plainly stands out as ____.
For decades, Pluto seemed to be the mysteriously ____ planet: it was first thought to be about as large as Earth, but, subsequently, measurements had it smaller and smaller.

Science is arguably a very high-minded pursuit, but that is not to say that all of its practitioners are ____, as numerous articles alleging overly generous pharmaceutical industry payments to medical researchers have tried to show.
